players.product: intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157) individualized neoantigen therapy, jointly developed with Merck

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jamey Mock: second-quarter total revenue was $145 million, up 2% from the prior year and above the guidance range given on the first-quarter call; geographic mix was 60% U.S. and 40% international. First-half revenue was $0.5 billion, 31% from the U.S. and 69% from international markets, with the long-term strategic partnerships driving the international contribution. CEO Stephane Bancel: the second quarter is always light for seasonal vaccines.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $145 million, up 2% year on year (60% U.S. / 40% international); first-half revenue $0.5 billion (31% U.S. / 69% international)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 cost of sales was $93 million, a 22% decrease from the prior year, primarily driven by lower unutilized manufacturing capacity costs as manufacturing efficiency improves; R&D expenses were $651 million, down 7%, on lower clinical development costs after the wind down of several late-stage programs; SG&A was $216 million, down 6%. Net loss was $782 million, improving by $43 million or 5%; loss per share was $1.97 versus $2.13 a year earlier. Cash and investments ended the quarter at $6.9 billion versus $7.5 billion at the end of Q1; in July the company paid $950 million related to the litigation settlement announced earlier this year, which will be reflected in the third-quarter cash balance. CEO: cash costs were reduced by 10% in Q2 compared to the second quarter of 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 cost of sales $93 million (-22%); R&D $651 million (-7%); SG&A $216 million (-6%); net loss $782 million; cash and investments $6.9 billion (Q1: $7.5 billion); $950 million litigation settlement paid in July

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 financial framework (CFO): total revenue still expected to grow up to 10% in 2026, with a roughly 50/50 split between U.S. and international revenue and third-quarter revenue approximately 55% of second-half revenue; the guidance factors in potential future declines in COVID vaccination rates and assumes no revenue from mFLUSIVA and mCOMBRIAX. Cost of sales projection lowered by $0.1 billion to $1.7 billion on additional manufacturing efficiency gains (including $0.9 billion of expense for the previously announced litigation settlement charge); R&D estimate lowered by $0.1 billion to $2.9 billion; SG&A still approximately $1 billion, flat. Excluding the $0.9 billion litigation charge, total GAAP operating expenses of $4.7 billion and cash costs of $4 billion, each a $0.2 billion improvement on the previous guidance; capital expenditures still $0.2 billion-$0.3 billion; year-end 2026 cash and investments now projected at $4.7 billion-$5.2 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue growth up to 10%; cost of sales $1.7 billion (lowered $0.1 billion); R&D $2.9 billion (lowered $0.1 billion); SG&A approximately $1 billion; GAAP opex $4.7 billion and cash costs $4 billion excluding the litigation charge (each $0.2 billion better); capex $0.2 billion-$0.3 billion; year-end cash $4.7 billion-$5.2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on the second half: first-half revenue was up almost $300 million versus the prior year, so being flat in the second half would put full-year growth above 10%. Internationally the company has basically contracted and must execute (some shipments could slip into the first quarter of the following year, which he called relatively small); this year it will supply some of its strategic partnerships in the second half, which is 'quite material' and offsets the U.S. vaccination-rate decline it has provided for (last year there was no U.K. volume in the second half). 'The biggest variable at this point is just what is the size of the U.S. market' - upside if the U.S. decline is smaller than projected, downside if worse. President Stephen Hoge: 2026 growth is driven by the long-term strategic partnerships in the U.K., Canada and Australia, supported by continued growth of mNEXSPIKE; over three years the company is building toward a broader portfolio including flu, the flu/COVID combination and norovirus plus late-stage oncology and rare disease programs.
quarterly_data.figure: first half up almost $300 million year on year; second-half strategic-partnership supply 'quite material'

quarterly_data.signal: Seasonal flu vaccine mRNA-1010 received a unanimous positive recommendation from the U.S. FDA VRBPAC advisory committee ahead of its August 5th PDUFA date; it is also under review in the European Union, Canada and Australia, and the phase III efficacy and safety results were published in The New England Journal of Medicine. CEO: the company anticipates approval for flu in Canada and Europe. Hoge: late strain selection was discussed with the FDA at the advisory committee - the company's demonstrated capability in the COVID context is less than two months, with strain selections as late as early July in the history of COVID - with public-health discussions on accommodating a late selection at an early stage; pricing is premature and subject to approval, but management views the product, given its relative vaccine efficacy versus standard dose and lack of egg adaptation, as in the enhanced category.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. PDUFA date August 5th; unanimous VRBPAC recommendation

quarterly_data.signal: COVID franchise (Hoge): mNEXSPIKE is now approved in the U.S., Europe, Canada, Australia, Japan and Taiwan, with additional filings planned for the second half of 2026. In its first season (2025-2026) mNEXSPIKE captured approximately 24% of the total U.S. retail COVID vaccine market and approximately 34% among individuals aged 65 and older; a real-world study found adjusted vaccine effectiveness against COVID hospitalization of approximately 59% in adults 65 and older and approximately 67% in adults 75 and older versus matched unvaccinated cohorts, numerically higher than a competitor vaccine in separately matched analysis (not designed as a head-to-head comparison). U.S. and European health authorities selected the XBB strain for the 2026-2027 season and the company is updating SPIKEVAX and mNEXSPIKE to target it.
quarterly_data.figure: mNEXSPIKE ~24% of U.S. retail COVID vaccine market (~34% among 65+); real-world effectiveness ~59% (65+) and ~67% (75+)

quarterly_data.signal: RSV vaccine mRESVIA: the company signed a joint procurement contract with the European Commission for up to 24 million doses of mRESVIA across six countries. mRESVIA is approved in 44 countries, most recently in Mexico for all adults aged 60 and older and high-risk adults aged 18-59, and received a label expansion in Australia to include high-risk adults aged 18-59.
quarterly_data.figure: European Commission joint procurement contract for up to 24 million doses across six countries; approved in 44 countries

quarterly_data.signal: Flu/COVID combination vaccine mCOMBRIAX is approved in the European Union and under review in Canada, Australia and Japan; in the U.S. the company awaits approval of its standalone flu vaccine before seeking further FDA guidance on refiling the combination. CEO: three products are on the market, mCOMBRIAX is a fourth approved product being prepared for launch in 2027, and flu is potentially a fifth approved in H2; Moderna has not been able to participate in the European market because of an exclusive partnership the EU set up during the pandemic, which expires in 2026, and Europe is seen as a very important growth driver. Hoge: health technology assessments have been submitted and pricing negotiations are under way, with first instances of pricing issued in a couple of countries; about half of the European markets are tender-related, some tenders covering 2027 and some 2028; management expects some contribution beginning in 2027 but the full effect probably not until 2028 and maybe a little beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: mCOMBRIAX launch prepared for 2027; European contribution expected to begin in 2027, full effect probably 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Partnerships: in Latin America the company advanced its strategic partnership in Brazil by signing an agreement with a local manufacturer to support its multi-year COVID vaccine supply agreement with the government; it also expanded its partnership with CEPI to explore the development of an Ebola vaccine.

Norovirus vaccine mRNA-1403: the phase III study did not meet the statistical criteria for early success at its interim analysis; the study remains blinded and the company is preparing to enroll an additional fourth cohort. Hoge: the trial enrolled, but primary-endpoint cases came more slowly (in the first season partly due to an outbreak of different norovirus strains not contributing to the primary endpoint), so the study, powered for a final analysis, is expected to run one more season this winter.
quarterly_data.figure: phase III interim did not meet early-success criteria; additional fourth cohort; one more season expected

quarterly_data.signal: Intismeran autogene (individualized neoantigen therapy developed in partnership with Merck) is advancing across nine phase II and phase III studies, per Chief Development Officer David Berman. The adjuvant melanoma phase III study is fully enrolled with the interim analysis expected in 2026 (second half; the company will issue a press release on the interim); the five-year phase II update with KEYTRUDA in adjuvant melanoma and translational data showing induction of de novo neoantigen-specific T cells (seven patients) were presented at ASCO 2026. Phase III studies run in adjuvant non-small cell lung cancer, including a newly initiated study testing intismeran as monotherapy and with KEYTRUDA QLEX. The adjuvant renal cell carcinoma phase II study, fully enrolled since the second quarter of 2025, could reach its analysis threshold this year or next; the muscle-invasive bladder cancer readout is more likely in 2027; the non-muscle invasive bladder cancer study continues to enroll; phase I adjuvant pancreatic and perioperative gastric studies are fully enrolled. Hoge: if the interim is positive the company would make the case for an accelerated review; a commercially valuable product could emerge maybe only at the final analysis.
quarterly_data.figure: nine phase II and phase III studies; melanoma phase III interim analysis expected in the second half of 2026; bladder readout more likely 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Hoge on intismeran launch readiness: the company has been establishing manufacturing in a dedicated facility in Massachusetts that will be able to support launch and, it believes, the commercial profile that Moderna and partner Merck have articulated for several years to come; it hopes to have to build more if demand is greater, and believes it can satisfy the initial indication from that facility and be ready to go next year if all went perfectly to plan. CEO: Moderna and Merck have been very active on medical affairs, marketing and commercial preparation, working hand in hand.
quarterly_data.figure: dedicated Massachusetts manufacturing facility to support launch; ready next year if all goes to plan

quarterly_data.signal: Berman on neoantigen selection: about 29% of the neoantigens that go into the company's cassettes are in general immunogenic, and the patients shown had between one and 18 reactive neoantigens each; the company has an ongoing program to improve its selection algorithm and is using artificial intelligence to try to develop the next algorithm, with an efficacy readout linking the algorithm to efficacy the next important step.
quarterly_data.figure: about 29% of cassette neoantigens immunogenic; one to 18 reactive neoantigens per patient

quarterly_data.signal: Other oncology programs (Berman): mRNA-4359 (IDO / PD-1) is in a phase II program in first-line and second-line-or-later metastatic melanoma and in first-line metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, with the ongoing phase II expansion meant to confirm the signal before deciding the path (more to come next year); dosing has begun with cancer antigen therapy mRNA-4200 alongside mRNA-4106 in a phase I study in advanced solid tumors; mRNA-4194 is dosing in a phase I/II study in Lynch syndrome; the T-cell engager mRNA-2808, described as the first three T-cell engagers in a single product, is dosing in a phase I/II study in relapsed refractory multiple myeloma; and with Immatics dosing continues in the phase I study of mRNA-4203 combined with the anzu-cel cell therapy.

Rare disease (Berman): the propionic acidemia (PA) registrational study is fully enrolled with around 20 patients; its primary endpoint, metabolic decompensation events on treatment relative to pretreatment with each patient as their own control, is based on 12-month follow-up and should occur sometime in the fourth quarter, with data expected in 2026; prior releases showed about 60%-80% efficacy. The pivotal-trial decision for methylmalonic acidemia (MMA) remains deferred until the PA readout. CEO: the company will work with a partner to ensure a great PA launch.
quarterly_data.figure: around 20 patients; 12-month follow-up primary endpoint expected in the fourth quarter; prior efficacy about 60%-80%
